one_line: Privacy-aware checkout that explains requested data and produces a privacy receipt.
what_it_does: A WebMCP-native checkout presents required and optional data, explains why it is requested, lets users minimize disclosure, and completes checkout after confirmation.
leverage_rationale: Structured read and write tools can expose privacy facts without personal values and enforce explicit confirmation, making agent checkout materially safer and more precise than UI driving.
leverage_evidence: Pitch explicitly distinguishes read-only privacy facts from personal form values.
Description claims the write tool completes checkout only after explicit confirmation.
execution_rationale: The concept and packaging are coherent, but there are no submitted frame sheets or transcript and the screenshot is only a paused Devpost video thumbnail; end-to-end checkout and receipt are not evidenced.
execution_evidence: Devpost screenshot shows a named project and demo thumbnail.
No product frame sheet or video transcript was submitted.
impact_rationale: Checkout data minimization and comprehensible privacy decisions address a real user need and an increasingly relevant agent safety problem.

one_line: A shared seating-chart board where humans set social constraints and agents solve arrangements.
what_it_does: Hosts drag guests, lock seats, express together/apart/at-table rules, and collaborate with an agent that proposes or solves seating while reporting violations.
leverage_rationale: The live shared state, locks, structured constraints, violation feedback, and solver are central to the product; a general UI-driving agent would be substantially less reliable and precise.
leverage_evidence: Pitch describes 15 tools over guest/table CRUD, constraints, violations, and auto-seat.

execution_rationale: The interface appears cohesive and covers the central workflow, though the evidence is a paused thumbnail plus frame sheets rather than an independently observed run.
execution_evidence: Frame sheet shows populated event-management screens and repeated workflow states.
Devpost thumbnail visibly shows seating groups, occupancy counts, locks, rules, violations, and agent activity.
impact_rationale: Event hosts face a real, complex constraint problem with sensitive social knowledge; the product directly reduces tedious arrangement work while preserving host authority.
impact_evidence: Description gives a concrete 24-person/5-table use case.
Human locks and agent refusal behavior preserve host decisions.
creativity_rationale: The two-player framing of seating—human social knowledge plus agent constraint solving on one board—is memorable and deeply pursued.
creativity_evidence: Bidirectional collaboration and activity feed are explicit design elements.
Constraint types, locked seats, and returned violation lists form a coherent interaction model.
usability_note: The visible board has clear table grouping, occupancy, rules, and violations; complexity may still be high for large events.
red_flags: No transcript and no live verification of the claimed 15 tools.
standouts: Strong shared-state human/agent design with human override and consequence feedback.
advance_reason: Excellent WebMCP fit and unusually complete evidence of a shared constraint-solving workflow.

one_line: A shared statistical research bench where agents run reproducible analyses from code and humans watch the evidence.
what_it_does: The agent loads data, builds signals, runs backtests and Fama-French regressions, while the page logs steps, renders charts, and exposes results to the human.
leverage_rationale: Shared live research state, executable analysis, logged steps, and code-grounded results make agent/human collaboration substantially more trustworthy than an agent merely narrating numbers through a UI.
leverage_evidence: Pitch describes data loading, signal construction, backtest, regression, chart rendering, and logged steps.

execution_evidence: Facts report a 186-second demo video.

impact_evidence: Project articulates the difficulty of trusting AI-generated R² and other results.

standouts: Strong trust/provenance thesis with a concrete shared-state research workflow.
advance_reason: One of the strongest concepts in the packet: high impact, high ambition, and transformative agent leverage.
